title: Madras HC restrains protests against SC order allowing lighting of lamp on Thiruparankundram hill

ai.summary: The Madras High Court restrained calls to defy the Supreme Court's order allowing lighting of the Karthigai Deepam lamp at Thiruparankundram hill, directing authorities to ensure compliance and release unlawfully detained individuals.

facts.claim: The Madras High Court restrained the public from calling for people to defy the Supreme Court’s order allowing the lighting of the Karthigai Deepam lamp at a stone pillar atop the Thiruparankundram hill in Tamil Nadu’s Madurai district
facts.quote: The Madras High Court on Tuesday restrained the public from calling for people to defy the Supreme Court’s Friday order allowing the lighting of the Karthigai Deepam lamp at a stone pillar atop the Thiruparankundram hill in Tamil Nadu’s Madurai district, Bar and Bench reported.

facts.claim: The court said its directions were limited to preventing calls to obstruct the implementation of the Supreme Court’s order
facts.quote: A bench of Justices GR Swaminathan and MD Sumathi clarified that while judicial orders could be criticised, including through strong remarks, no one should call for their non-compliance.

facts.claim: The court directed the Madurai collector to ignore any advice to defy the Supreme Court’s directions, even if it came from another authority
facts.quote: The High Court directed the Madurai collector to ignore any advice to defy the Supreme Court’s directions, “even if it came from another authority”.

facts.claim: The court said that the prohibitory order issued by the collector under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita must not interfere with devotees’ fundamental right to practise their religion under Article 25 of the Constitution
facts.quote: The court also said that the prohibitory order issued by the collector under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita must not interfere with devotees’ fundamental right to practise their religion under Article 25 of the Constitution, Live Law reported.

facts.claim: The court further directed the authorities to release anyone unlawfully detained under the order
facts.quote: The court further directed the authorities to release anyone unlawfully detained under the order.

facts.claim: The administration said that 258 persons who were 'connected to certain organisations' had been detained and two first information reports were registered
facts.quote: The administration said that 258 persons who were 'connected to certain organisations' had been detained and two first information reports were registered.

ai.background_note: The Madras High Court upheld the Supreme Court's order to allow lighting of the Karthigai Deepam lamp at Thiruparankundram hill, but the Tamil Nadu government has filed a review petition challenging the order.
